mercy_translation.text:
The death on the cross, then, was fitting and appropriate on our behalf, and its reason has been shown to be reasonable in every respect. There are sound grounds for saying that the salvation of all had to take place through the cross and not otherwise.

Even there, upon the cross, he did not leave himself without witness. Rather, beyond expectation he made creation bear witness to the presence of its Creator. And he did not allow his own temple, the body, to remain dead for long. Having only shown it dead through its encounter with death, he immediately raised it on the third day, bearing as trophies and victories over death the incorruption and impassibility manifested in the body.

For he could have raised the body immediately from death and shown it alive again, but the Savior, wisely foreseeing the matter, did not do this. Someone might then have said that it had not died at all, or that death had not fully touched it, if he had immediately displayed the resurrection.

Perhaps also, if death and resurrection had occurred at exactly the same instant, the glory of incorruption would have remained unclear. Therefore, so that the body might be shown truly dead, the Word allowed one intervening day and on the third day showed it incorruptible to all.

Thus, in order that death in the body should be demonstrated, he raised it on the third day.

But so that, if he waited a long time and then raised a body already corrupted, he might not be disbelieved as though carrying another body rather than the same one—for someone might have doubted what he saw because of the passage of time and forgotten what had happened—he did not wait more than three days or keep those who had heard him speak about the resurrection in suspense for long.

While the word was still sounding in their ears, while their eyes were still expecting, while their minds remained fixed on it, and while those who had killed the Lord's body and witnessed its death were still alive on earth and present in those places, the Son of God himself, after an interval of three days, showed the body that had been dead to be immortal and incorruptible. And it was evident to all that the body had not died because of weakness in the nature of the indwelling Word, but so that death might be abolished in it by the power of the Savior.

translator_notes: Translated directly from the Greek source.
Athanasius uses the three-day interval to defend both the reality of death and the identity/continuity of the risen body.
The resurrection is presented as the public manifestation of death's defeat and the body's incorruption.
